title: Precise Energy Consumption Measurements of Heterogeneous Artificial Intelligence Workloads
benchmark_measurement: The paper does not measure anything related to faith or religion. It measures the energy consumption and performance (runtime, power draw) of two deep learning models (an LSTM for time-series forecasting and a CNN for image classification) on different types of heterogeneous compute nodes (CPU-only, GPU, mixed CPU/GPU).
findings: This paper does not contain any findings related to religion. The key findings are about the energy efficiency of AI workloads on different hardware. For instance, it finds that for image-related tasks, GPUs are superior in both runtime and energy consumption for training and inference. For sequential data tasks, inference on CPUs can be comparably energy-efficient to GPUs. It also highlights that the energy consumption of idle GPUs on mixed-use nodes is significant and should not be neglected.
